claims.text: Conventional untreated stainless steel has limited corrosion endurance under extreme conditions.
A TiN coating can be deposited on stainless steel using Physical Vapor Deposition.
PVD-deposited TiN enhances the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
The deposited TiN coating forms a thin, dense, and uniform surface layer.
The TiN surface layer is chemically inert under the proposed corrosive conditions.
The TiN layer acts as a protective barrier that limits penetration of corrosive species.
Limiting the ingress of moisture and aggressive ions reduces localized chemical reactions and degradation of the stainless-steel substrate.
Unmodified stainless steel undergoes accelerated corrosion in high-temperature molten salts or aggressive acids.
PVD TiN-coated stainless steel will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated stainless steel under identical harsh conditions.
PVD TiN-coated stainless steel will maintain its mechanical integrity under the proposed harsh conditions.
The corrosion-protection improvement depends on coating thickness, uniformity, adhesion quality, and the corrosive environment.
